stories.headline: Ilhan Omar should be jailed, deported if citizenship fraud proven, Top House Republican says
stories.note: House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, Minnesota's top House Republican, says Ilhan Omar should face jail and deportation if the federal probe proves she or her father lied to get her citizenship.
body: Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota is under federal investigation over claims that she or her father misstated her birth year on immigration paperwork when the family came from Somalia in the late 1990s. Federal agents searched her Washington, D.C., home earlier this week and took her phone and other belongings.

The question is her age. Her father became a citizen in 2000, and Omar, believed to be 17 then, would have qualified automatically as a minor. The allegation is that she was really 18, which would have required her to apply on her own.

In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, the No. 3 House Republican and the highest-ranking House member from Omar's state, said there have been rumors about her for years. If they're proven, he said, she should serve time and then be sent back where she came from.

Emmer rejected the claim that the probe is political. He noted that a judge had to find probable cause of a federal crime before signing the search warrant. "Maybe after all these years, someone is finally going to hold Ilhan Omar accountable," he said.

Omar called the raid an attempt to weaponize law enforcement against Trump's critics and vowed she would not be silenced. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and his deputies called it deeply disturbing, and allies note it comes less than three weeks before the Nov. 3 election.
Why it matters: A Squad member facing a court-approved citizenship fraud investigation puts Democrats on defense in the final stretch, and GOP leaders are making clear they won't let it slide.

stories.headline: ICE arrests more than 100 alleged gang members in single week, including violent MS-13, TdA suspects: DHS
stories.note: DHS says ICE nabbed 131 alleged gang members in a single week, including 22 tied to MS-13 and 13 to Tren de Aragua, bringing gang arrests under Trump past 12,000.
body: ICE agents arrested 131 gang-affiliated people who are in the country illegally between Oct. 4 and Oct. 10, the Department of Homeland Security told Fox News Digital. That included 22 linked to MS-13 and 13 linked to Tren de Aragua.

DHS says ICE has now made 12,018 gang-related arrests since President Trump returned to office in 2025. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin credited Trump's leadership and said deporting illegal aliens, especially gang members, "is how we make America safe again."

Among those picked up was a Salvadoran man DHS identifies as an MS-13 member, arrested in Las Vegas. He's wanted in El Salvador on charges including aggravated homicide and rape of a minor, and he had already been deported once in 2021 before coming back illegally.

Agents also arrested a Venezuelan described as a suspected Tren de Aragua hitman in Tallahassee. DHS says he crossed in October 2023 under President Biden, was caught by Border Patrol, and was released into the country. In Washington, D.C., ICE arrested a suspected MS-13 member released after crossing in 2012 under President Obama, with a record that includes attempted murder and armed robbery arrests.
In Denver, agents arrested a 14-year-old Venezuelan tied to a Tren de Aragua faction who faces an attempted first-degree murder charge and was carrying a Glock pistol, according to DHS.

Why it matters: The arrests show the Trump enforcement push clearing out dangerous gang members, several of whom were released under Biden and Obama, and give Republicans a concrete public safety contrast heading into November.

stories.headline: Dem congressional candidate's police record reveals suspensions over stolen gun, insubordination
stories.note: Texas Democrat Johnny Garcia built his House campaign on his sheriff's deputy career, but records show two unpaid suspensions, including one after his gun and badge were stolen from his car.
body: Johnny Garcia, the Democratic nominee in Texas' newly redrawn 35th District, was suspended without pay twice while serving with the Bexar County Sheriff's Office, according to records Fox News Digital obtained through a public records request.

In 2009, he got a three-day suspension for insubordination after repeatedly carrying his cellphone into a secure jail area despite being told not to. In 2020, he got five days for job performance after leaving his Glock, four magazines and his badge in his car, where they were stolen. The gun was later recovered.

The Sheriff's Office confirmed both suspensions and said Garcia faced no other discipline over the incidents. His law enforcement career is a centerpiece of his centrist pitch, along with border security, which his website says Biden failed on.

Garcia is running against Republican Carlos De La Cruz, an Air Force veteran, for the seat Rep. Greg Casar is leaving. Casar won the old district with about 67% in 2024, but Texas Republicans redrew the map last year and Casar moved to the neighboring 37th District.
Garcia's campaign called the claims politicized and a Republican attempt to distract, pointing to his nearly two decades protecting his community.
Why it matters: Garcia is a first-time candidate in a seat Republicans redrew to compete for, and records undercutting his main selling point could help De La Cruz flip it on Nov. 3.

stories.headline: 'No Kings' foot soldiers ignore organizers' warning, go all in for Democrats
stories.note: A Fox News Digital investigation finds local 'No Kings' groups pushing 'Vote Blue' and Democratic canvassing at today's rallies, despite the national organizers' own ban on partisan messaging.
body: Today's "No Kings" events are billed as a nonpartisan, nationwide get-out-the-vote push, and the national coalition's rulebook bans partisan messaging, including "vote Blue" and "vote them out" appeals, candidate activity, and coordination with political parties.

A Fox News Digital investigation found local organizers ignoring those rules. An Indivisible chapter in Newark, Delaware, suggested signs like "Time for a Blue Tsunami," an Oregon chapter suggested "Republicans had their chance!", and the Placer County Democratic Party in California advertised canvassing for its endorsed candidates tied to a rally at the Roseville Galleria.

Fox reports the effort is led by Indivisible, which has received millions from Democratic megadonor George Soros, within a network of about 300 groups with an estimated $2.5 billion in annual revenue running roughly 3,000 events. Partners include the major teachers and public-employee unions, MoveOn, Planned Parenthood Action Fund and the Democratic Socialists of America.

Indivisible co-founder Ezra Levin was openly partisan in recent webinars, saying "our candidates are quite good" while Republican candidates are "quite trash," and describing a goal of a Democratic trifecta by 2029. He told one chapter to make its event about Trump.
The distinction matters legally: federal law bars 501(c)(3) charities from supporting or opposing candidates. "No Kings" organizers did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.
Why it matters: The reporting undercuts the movement's nonpartisan branding and suggests a tax-exempt-backed protest network is functioning as a Democratic turnout machine weeks before the midterms.

stories.headline: Democrats' latest gun-control push runs into inconvenient fact about how school killer was stopped
stories.note: Democrats demanded new gun laws after the Oregon school shooting, but the killer used his mother's shotgun in a gun-free zone and was stopped by an armed dad.
body: After a teenage gunman killed three children and a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, Democrats including Sen. Ron Wyden, Rep. Janelle Bynum and Sen. Jack Reed called for new gun laws, with Reed also taking aim at the Supreme Court's gun-rights rulings.

Gun-rights advocates point to how the attack unfolded. The shooter reportedly used a shotgun his mother bought, and he was pursued into the school and fatally shot by Kaylub Giamanco, an armed father of two students there. The district bans firearms, including concealed guns.

"What did stop the mass murderer and save lives was an armed bystander with good aim," said Aidan Johnston of Gun Owners of America. The NRA noted Oregon already has nearly every gun-control measure on the wish list, and argued background checks and red-flag laws likely wouldn't have stopped a teen who got a family member's gun.

Researcher John Lott said gun-free zones draw attackers, citing his group's finding that armed civilians stopped more active shootings than police from 2014 through 2024. He pointed to a 2021 Oregon law letting districts ban concealed carry by permit holders, which he estimates about 25 of 197 districts have done.
Even Rep. Bynum acknowledged the bystander's bravery at a vigil. Investigators are still examining how the teen got access to the shotgun.
Why it matters: The facts of the case cut against the Democratic push for new restrictions and bolster the Republican case that armed, law-abiding citizens save lives.

stories.headline: Obama's star power gets a reality check from Black voters in crucial Senate race: 'It's a turnoff'
stories.note: Obama's endorsement of Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed isn't moving undecided Black voters in Detroit, opening a door for Republican Mike Rogers in a toss-up Senate race.
body: Former President Obama has endorsed Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan, and the two are set to campaign together. Fox News Digital interviewed more than a dozen Black voters in Detroit to see whether that helps.

Most said they plan to back El-Sayed, but several undecided voters said Obama's support didn't sway them. One called it "a turn-off" because she has seen too many candidates use Obama to work the Democratic vote, and another said he didn't want to be pushed toward a candidate because someone else backs him.

Some voters also questioned the pairing because El-Sayed wrote a 2012 column blasting Obama over wars, civil liberties and deportations, calling his reelection "no victory." El-Sayed has since walked those criticisms back. Roughly half of those interviewed said the endorsement improved their view, though none had been undecided before it.

The interviews echo other warning signs: a late-September Fox News poll showed El-Sayed at just 77% among Black voters, well below the usual Democratic benchmark, and an MS NOW focus group found similar reluctance. A Detroit ally of El-Sayed pushed back, saying enthusiasm grows as voters learn about him.

Republican nominee Mike Rogers is courting disaffected Democrats, including Black voters in Detroit. Fox News Power Rankings rate the race a toss-up. Obama and El-Sayed's campaign didn't respond to requests for comment.
Why it matters: Democrats can't win Michigan statewide without strong Detroit turnout, and soft support there gives Rogers a real opening to flip the seat.

stories.headline: Income inequality at Obama Foundation, as brass thrives and rank and file seeks union
stories.note: Obama Foundation CEO Valerie Jarrett made $771,000 and half the staff earn six figures, while rank-and-file workers say benefits were cut and are trying to unionize.
body: The Obama Foundation paid CEO Valerie Jarrett $771,000 in 2025, according to its tax filing reviewed by Fox News Digital, and 172 of its 342 reported employees, about half, made more than $100,000.

That share is higher than at the other presidential foundations Fox reviewed, from 37% at the George W. Bush Presidential Center down to 10% at the George & Barbara Bush Foundation, and Jarrett's pay tops all five of their CEOs. Several top earners are former Obama White House or campaign aides, including Michelle Obama's former chief of staff at about $431,000.

Payroll and benefits hit $50.4 million in 2025, up from $18.5 million in 2018, as the long-delayed Obama Presidential Center's price tag climbed to about $1 billion, nearly triple the original estimate.

Meanwhile, workers organizing with AFSCME, including visitor services, cleaning, museum and program staff, say their benefits have been rolled back amid growing workloads. The foundation says it pays market rates, that its board sets executive pay using comparison data, and that it supports workers' right to organize.

Illinois GOP Chairman Bob Grogan called the center a political operation that uses taxpayer dollars "to make Barack Obama's inner circle rich." The foundation says construction was privately funded, though public money has paid for surrounding infrastructure.
Why it matters: Big paychecks at the top and union complaints at the bottom make an awkward picture for a Democratic icon whose party campaigns on income inequality.
